title: Hackers Use Chinese AI Tool to Hit South Korean Banks, Exposing New Risk
key_facts: At least 68,000 people's personal data reportedly exposed in breaches of at least seven financial institutions
Officials believe the Chinese cybersecurity tool Artex AI was used
Institutions named include Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank (about 25,000 Shinhan customers reportedly affected)
33 IP addresses found, linked to at least 12 countries, per local reports citing the Financial Supervisory Service
Incidents first came to light on 30 Sep; The Record calls them the first known AI-agent hacks of the financial sector
President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 that signs of AI use have emerged
National Office of Investigation formed a team of 28 investigators
quote_evidence: The personal data of at least 68,000 people was reportedly exposed in breaches of at least seven financial institutions, with officials saying they believe the Chinese cybersecurity tool Artex AI was used to hack the banks’ systems.
“Signs have emerged” suggesting AI agents were deployed in at least some of the attacks, Lee said Tuesday.
why_it_matters_hint: Largest reported AI-linked attack on financial customers' data so far, still under investigation.
notes: WSJ original blocked (HTTP 401); story written from The Record. Earlier editions: 4, 5 and 6 Oct 2026 on the same breaches.
